Theme

Church life

chant noun and verb

in church

also plainchant, plainsong, Gregorian chant, Byzantine chant

classical

M-O s.v. Gregorian chant: cantus Grēgoriānus, after Du Cange’s cantus ecclēsiasticus

cantus, cantūs m.

noun, fourth declension

singing, chant

Church chant is cantus ecclēsiasticus (Du Cange), the Western plainchant cantus Grēgoriānus (M-O; the ē is the eta of Greek Γρηγόριος); the Byzantine and Slavonic chant of the Orthodox Church has no Latin name in these sources.

Other words

  • canō, canere, cecinī, cantum — sing, chant

    verb, third conjugation · classical · Ambr. hymn. Deus creātor 12: hymnum canentēs solvimus

  • psallō, psallere, psallī — sing psalms, chant

    verb, third conjugation · also used · late Latin · Vulg. 1 Cor. 14.15 (Lewis & Short); Vulg. Ps. 103 (104), 33

    Classically to play the cithara, or sing to it (Sall. Cat. 25.2; Hor.).

Examples

  • Cantābō Dominō in vītā meā; psallam Deō meō quamdiū sum.

    I will sing to the Lord all my life; I will sing psalms to my God while I live.Vulg. Ps. 103 (104), 33

See also hymn, psalm, sing, chant.
